visualCharacteristics: One Everviz chart, chart layout or table (formerly Highcharts Cloud) in a <figure>, in a ~960px column centred in the content column
Default renders inline with the Everviz inject script, like seic.com; the chart sizes itself to the column and reflows on mobile
While the script loads, the chart's space is reserved (400px or the Height row) on a light-grey panel so the page does not shift
Optional caption under the chart: small slate text (body-font-size-s), links and emphasis kept
If the chart cannot load (deleted chart, blocked script, nothing rendered in 10s) a bordered box with a 'View chart' link to the Everviz embed page replaces it; the caption stays
iframe option embeds the Everviz embed page in a lazy, borderless, full-width iframe (500px tall or the Height row)
wide fills the content column (1280px max); narrow is a ~720px reading column
contentPattern: Rows in any order; empty rows are ignored

Chart row (required, normally row 1): an Everviz URL in any form (https://app.everviz.com/inject/<id>/, /embed/<id>/, a share link, a pasted seic.com embed snippet), as a link or plain text; a bare chart id (e.g. r9SKBTsZ_) is accepted in the first row. A `Chart | <url or id>` labelled row also works
Optional `Caption | text` row, or any other unlabelled text: the figcaption (the authored paragraph is moved, so it stays editable)
Optional `Alt | text` (or `Description | text`) row: accessible description of the chart, read by screen readers (aria-describedby), not shown
Optional `Height | 600` row: chart height in px (iframe height; reserved space while the inject script loads)
Without a recognisable chart URL or id the block renders nothing
usage: Embed Everviz charts, chart layouts and tables in Document Authoring pages, matching how seic.com embeds them in article rich text (46 seic.com insight and factor-sheet pages, 77 chart ids; see migration-work/everviz-inventory.json).
reuseGuidance: Use for any chart built in Everviz (app.everviz.com). Default inject mode matches seic.com and lets the chart use the page width; use iframe when the inline script conflicts with something on the page or the same chart appears twice. For a chart drawn from a table authored in the document use bar-chart; for a static chart image use image.
